130-(use `codex` in place of `claude-code` on Codex):
131-
132-```bash
133-gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json   # the resolved target; writes nothing

135-```

138-prints init's first-run decision bundle once, after the wiring and its smoke
139-check (an `[AGENT]` block in human output, `notices` in `--json`), without
140-`harness_wiring`, which setup just did. Relay the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5)
141-and the other settings in the reply that reports the install, as the settings
142-in effect and how to change them; nothing waits on the answer, so don't end
143-the install on a question, and apply an answer with its option's command
144-whenever the user gives one. Capture
145-(`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts
146-them. A coded refusal (`setup_owner_conflict`, `setup_hosted_connection`) means
147-another owner or a hosted brain holds the target; follow its `fix`.
148-When the brain will answer several people (a team bot, a shared channel), ask the
149-user who they are and add `--serves several --members <id,...>`: each gets a member,
150-a folder `people/<member>/` only they read and a bound key
151-(`~/.gbrain/member-keys/<member>.key`; relay paths, never keys). On
152-`setup_serves_several`, rerun with its fix. Add `--stdio-member <member>`
153-(claude-code, codex) only for a harness one person uses. Doctor's
154-`unlabeled_people_folders` names a person's folder without a rule.
155-`--remove` undoes only what setup wrote. Guide:
156-[docs/guides/setup.md](docs/guides/setup.md). Otherwise:
157-
158-```bash
159-gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding     # keyless memory, no server needed
160-gbrain doctor --json                   # inspect diagnostics and any warnings
161-```
162-
163-**The first-run settings.** Init applies its defaults and exits 0; nothing waits
164-for an answer. When no agent is connected yet it prints a `harness_wiring`
165-notice: connecting gbrain to the agent you run in is part of the install, so do
166-it now (Step 5), not after the user replies. It also prints the settings in
167-effect once, as an `[AGENT]` block (`gbrain init --json`: a notice of kind

169-
170-| Setting | What the user can change | In effect |

173-| `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | off; gbrain recommends `salient`, which the user opts into |
174-| `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip |
175-| `upkeep` | free upkeep while the agent's session is open | on |
176-
177-Connect first, then report the install and relay the bundle's `user_message`
178-in that reply, as the settings in effect and how to change them. Apply an
179-answer with the command its option names whenever the user gives one. Details:
180-[first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run).

281:## Step 3.5: Tell the user which search mode is in effect (DO NOT SKIP)
282-
283-This is the `search_mode` setting from the first-run settings.
284-`gbrain init` auto-applied a default search mode: `tokenmax` with a chat key
285-(Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), `balanced` with a ready reranker but no chat key,
286-and `conservative` when your subagent tier is Haiku-class or neither exists. The init output
287-included the cost matrix below preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. Don't accept it
288-silently, and don't stop the install to ask either: on every harness, connect
289-gbrain first (with `gbrain setup <harness>` or the `harness_wiring` step), then
290-show the matrix and the applied mode in the reply that reports the install, as
291-a choice the user can make at any time, and run
292-`gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` when they pick one.
293-
294-If you already know the operator's choice, record it at install time instead:
295-`gbrain init --search-mode <conservative|balanced|tokenmax>` stores it as the
296-operator's (`search.mode_source: operator`) and init asks no `search_mode`
297-question. On an existing brain with a different mode it refuses unless you pass
298-`--force`.
299-
300-**Present this matrix verbatim:**
301-
302-<!-- Cost matrix: generated by costMatrixLines() in src/core/search/mode-advice.ts (prices from src/core/model-pricing.ts); test/init-mode-picker.test.ts keeps this block in sync. -->
303-```
304-Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:
305-
306-                  Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
307-                  ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
308-  conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
309-  balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
310-  tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo
311-
312-  Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
313-  Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
314-  Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.
315-```
316-
317-**Ask the operator (paraphrase if needed):**
318-
319-> Your gbrain is installed and connected, with search mode
320-> `<auto-applied default>`. It controls retrieval payload size, and you can
321-> change it any time. The modes:
322->
323->   1) conservative — tight 4K budget, 10 chunks max, no reranker.
324->      Best for Haiku subagents, cost-sensitive setups, high-volume loops.
325->
326->   2) balanced — 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked.
327->
328->   3) tokenmax (recommended with a chat key) — no budget, 50 chunks, reranked.
329->      The widest retrieval.
330->
331-> `gbrain query` does not expand by default in any mode; `--expand`
332-> (`expand: true` over MCP) forces it and `--no-expand` (`expand: false`) skips
333-> it. `gbrain config set search.expansion true` turns the default on for the
334-> brain in any mode. `gbrain search` and the memory
335-> verbs never expand. See [search modes](docs/guides/search-modes.md) for the
336-> current contract.
337->

  brain      new keyless PGLite brain at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite (gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding)
  source     the brain's default source (unpinned)
  transport  stdio MCP: /harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs (lists the memory verbs and request_tools; every starter tool stays callable)

  313 migration(s) applied
[setup] Migrations: 14 recorded as not needed on a new brain; 5 setup migration(s) applied by setup without installing services (0.11.0, 0.14.0, 0.22.4, 0.28.0, 0.53.0); none pending.
Fresh brain setup approves following the packaged memory skills: prose only, existing memory/discovery tools, no scripts, paid services, capture or editor grants.
[init] Using schema pack: gbrain-base-v2 (override with --schema-pack <name>)
{"phase":"search_mode_picker","mode":"conservative","reason":"No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.","auto":true,"source":"auto"}
Brain ready at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite
  write    receipt /harness-state/claude/.gbrain-connection-claude-code-gbrain.json (prepared: consent and pending hashes recorded)
  write    mcp     'gbrain' in /harness-state/claude/.claude.json
  write    hooks   SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit in /harness-state/claude/settings.json
  write    instructions brain-first block in new file /harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md [default; opt out with --no-instructions]
Verify: ok (smoke_passed): initialize, tools/list (8 tools) and recall answered.
Turn hook: ok (ran): UserPromptSubmit hook in /harness-state/claude/settings.json; it ran and added the rule
State: native-pending (configured -> connection-verified -> native-pending). Native push is not claimed until an observed event reaches a fresh session.
Next: open a new Claude Code session (config is read at session start) and check that /mcp lists gbrain.
Memory: save what the user asks you to remember as a fact with gbrain remember "<fact>", naming its entity and provenance (MCP tool: remember). World-visible facts (the default) are pushed into new sessions; a private fact is not (local CLI recall only). capture writes a page, not a fact.
Opt-ins (nothing is on until you turn it on): keys and embeddings, autopilot, dream schedule, connectors, auto-upgrade, release channel: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.734.0/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#opt-ins
[AGENT]
why: [first_run_decisions] Setup is complete: the brain is ready and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. These first-run settings are in effect as listed; none blocks memory or needs a new session to answer. Relay them once, in the reply that reports this install, as the current settings and how to change them; do not hold the install open or end it waiting on an answer. When the user picks an option, run its command. Automatic saving (`writeback`) is separate from setup's capture decision (Stop/SessionEnd hooks); while unanswered it comes back in a later session until the user answers or mutes it.
1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)
   - conservative: conservative (applied) (run: gbrain config set search.mode conservative)
   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.
2. Should agents save important facts the user states (preferences, decisions, commitments) automatically, with provenance? Saved facts are readable by agents connected to this brain; transient facts expire. Off any time with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off`. (id: writeback)
   - salient: Save durable facts the user states directly (recommended) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient)
   - all: Every direct factual statement (more low-value facts, more extraction spend) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback all)
   - off: Save only what the user explicitly asks to remember (records the answer) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off)
   default: off — In effect now: agents save only what the user asks them to remember. salient is recommended for a personal brain; it is opt-in, so it turns on only when the user picks it.
3. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. (id: upkeep)
   - on: Keep free upkeep on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn free upkeep off (run: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false)
   default: on — In effect now: the agent's gbrain serve runs the free upkeep tier while idle; nothing needs an answer.
4. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. (id: conversation_archive)
   - on: Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.
5. Give this brain a shape? A personal brain gets three empty starter pages (facts about you, your voice, how you decide) and a notes folder you pick, imported read only. A company brain gets empty pages for company facts, decisions, pricing, customers, calls and playbooks in a company source, and a docs folder you pick. Setup tells the agent to read them. Nothing is invented. (id: brain_shape)
   - personal: Personal brain, no notes folder yet (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal)
   - company: Company brain, just me (add --docs <folder> for company docs, --transcripts <folder> for call transcripts) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company)
   - both: Personal and company brain, just me (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape both)
   - company_team: Company brain shared with a team (prints where it lives; creates nothing) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company --team)
   - none: No starter pages (memory works as it is)
   default: none — Nothing is written until the user picks; memory already works without it.
[SHOW USER]
gbrain is set up and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. In effect: search mode conservative; agents save only what you ask them to remember, until you turn on automatic saving (salient is recommended: durable facts you state, saved with provenance). Report back (Wakeshift): off. gbrain wakeshift enable turns it on. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $16…
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]

[SHOW USER]
Hosted option: gbrain.io runs GBrain for you, with nothing to keep online, and can import this brain: https://gbrain.io/?ref=cli-setup. Mute: gbrain notices mute hosted_option.

content.content:
# Ambient memory writeback

Ambient recall ([ambient-recall.md](./ambient-recall.md)) is the READ side of
memory: context arrives at session boundaries without a question being asked.
This guide is the WRITE side: when the brain's operator opts in, agents save
salient facts the user states directly — during ordinary conversation, without
being told to — through the existing MEMORY_VERBS surface. No new protocol
verb; `remember` and `extract_facts` do all the writing.

**Say to your agent:** *"Turn on ambient memory writeback for my brain"* —
*"remember things I tell you without being asked"* — your agent runs
`gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient` and
`gbrain bootstrap harness --yes`.

Off by default. Nothing in this feature ever enables itself.

The [conversation archive](./conversation-archive.md) is a separate lane: it
keeps the sessions themselves (one redacted page per conversation per day), is
on by default on a personal brain, extracts no facts, and is turned off with
`gbrain transcripts archive off`; `memory.auto_writeback` does not change it.

## Who gets asked (and who is never asked)

gbrain distinguishes PERSONAL brains from company/team brains and only ever
*offers* ambient writeback on personal ones — capturing what people say to
agents on a shared brain is a privacy decision the whole team owns, not a
default.

- **Declaration wins.** `brain.audience` (`personal` | `shared`) is the
  declared axis: set it yourself, let `company-brainify` stamp `shared` at its
  Phase-5 handoff, or answer the bootstrap interview. A declaration always
  beats the heuristic.
- **The heuristic is conservative.** Without a declaration, only ≥3 distinct
  non-automation MCP clients active in the last 30 days reads as shared
  evidence (client count measures surface breadth, not people — Claude Code +
  Codex + a phone client is one human). `gbrain doctor`'s `memory_writeback`
  check shows the resolved audience and its reasons; correct a
  misclassification with `gbrain config set brain.audience personal|shared`.
- **The ask fires once.** On personal brains, `gbrain init` and the
  post-upgrade banner print a one-time `[AGENT]`-relayed disclosure + ask
  (sentinel `memory.auto_writeback_notice_shown`); declining is permanent.
  `gbrain advisor` keeps a quiet reminder afterward — informational only,
  never `--apply`-able: consent is never automated.
- **Silence everywhere else:** shared/unknown brains, mounted team brains,
  thin clients, remote MCP callers, and any classifier failure.
- Explicitly enabling on a shared-classified brain works (operator
  sovereignty) but prints a caution: members' words get persisted into a
  store other authorized agents can read.

## Modes

| `memory.auto_writeback` | What agents are told to save |
|---|---|
| unset (default) | Nothing — no instruction section, no Stop-hook backstop, no banking. The compaction harvest and SessionEnd transcripts still extract; see [Capture lanes and the off switch](#capture-lanes-and-the-off-switch). |
| `off` | Nothing, and every ambient capture lane stops: the compaction harvest and SessionEnd transcripts too. |
| `salient` (recommended) | Durable, notable claims only: preferences, corrections, decisions, commitments, relationships, project-state changes. The backstop keeps medium+ notability facts. |
| `all` | Every direct factual user statement — still excluding operational chatter, assistant-generated content, secrets/credentials, and quoted third-party material. Precision rides the extractor's semantic skip rules (the second of the two filters); expect more low-value facts and more extraction spend. |

Both planes carry the setting: `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback …`

gbrain is set up as a free local brain connected to Claude Code, with no API keys. Its built-in test passed: the connection started, listed 8 memory tools and answered a recall. `claude mcp get gbrain` also shows it as **Connected**.

**What I ran:** `gbrain setup claude-code` with its defaults, after a dry run to check what it would write. It created and changed:
- a local brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`, which needs no server and no embedding key
- a `gbrain` memory-tool server entry in `~/.claude/.claude.json`
- two hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` that pull in memory context when a session starts and when you send a message
- a short rule in a new `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` telling the agent to check the brain first

It left off transcript capture and paid providers.

**To use it:** start a new Claude Code session, because this one won't load the new config. `/mcp` should then list gbrain.

**`gbrain doctor`:** it scored 95/100. The one warning says Claude Code has no gbrain registration, but `claude mcp get` shows it registered and connected. I expect the warning to clear once a new session has used it.

**Settings now in effect:**

| Setting | Current | To change |
|---|---|---|
| Search mode | `conservative` (4K token budget, no reranker), the right choice with no keys | `gbrain config set search.mode balanced` or `tokenmax`; both work much better with a key |
| Automatic saving | off: facts are saved only when you ask | `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient` |
| Free upkeep | on while a session is open | `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false` |
| Conversation archive | on: one redacted page per conversation per day; nothing leaves this machine without a key | `gbrain transcripts archive off` |
| Starter pages | none | `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal` |

I left automatic saving off even though gbrain recommends `salient`. Its docs say that consent has to come from you, so it's your call.

Search mode controls how much text the agent pulls in per query. gbrain's estimate at 10,000 queries a month:

| Mode | Haiku 5.5 | Sonnet 5.5 | Opus 5.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| conservative | $4 | $80 | $160 |
| balanced | $10 | $200 | $400 |
| tokenmax | $20 | $400 | $800 |

That's input to whatever model you already run; gbrain itself charges nothing. If you'd rather not keep a machine running, gbrain.io offers a hosted version that can import this brain.
